speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where you feel the weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm, and tell me if this started suddenly or gradually. To help narrow this down, do you have any history of recent neck injury, repetitive strain, or new neurological symptoms elsewhere?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor (superior sulcus tumor). 

The combination of progressive arm weakness, sensory loss, significant weight loss, and a history of heavy smoking strongly suggests an apical lung malignancy compressing the lower brachial plexus.
